# Contribute and verify

Start with the [repository map](README.md#where-desired-state-lives).
Run commands from the checkout root with Nix flakes enabled. Evaluation
may build import-from-derivation inputs; use a compatible builder even
for inspection. Do not accept new cache keys or PR-provided Nix settings
automatically.

## Choose the smallest relevant check

Use the platform inventory below to find a check's name, runtime needs
and hosted support. Build an individual check with:

```sh
nix build --no-link -L "path:.#checks.$system.$check"
```

Set `system` to the builder's native platform and `check` to the selected
inventory entry. A runtime check can need KVM, UID-range support or
cgroups; read its requirements before running it. Use disposable native
Linux builders for host/recovery fixtures. Never run fixtures against
production Docker, Incus, mounts or credentials, and never weaken host
isolation to make a fixture run.

### `aarch64-darwin`

Inspect check capabilities and unsupported reasons, then build the hosted
non-runtime checks on a builder for this platform:

```sh
nix eval --json path:.#hostedCiPlan.aarch64-darwin.inventory
nix build --no-link -L path:.#hostedCiJobs.aarch64-darwin.checks
```

Buildable output groups: `checks`, `darwinConfigurations`, `devShells`, `formatters`, `homeConfigurations`, `nixosConfigurations`, `packages`.
Build one with `nix build --no-link -L path:.#ciJobs.aarch64-darwin.<group>`.

### `aarch64-linux`

Inspect check capabilities and unsupported reasons, then build the hosted
non-runtime checks on a builder for this platform:

```sh
nix eval --json path:.#hostedCiPlan.aarch64-linux.inventory
nix build --no-link -L path:.#hostedCiJobs.aarch64-linux.checks
```

Buildable output groups: `checks`, `darwinConfigurations`, `devShells`, `formatters`, `homeConfigurations`, `nixosConfigurations`, `packages`.
Build one with `nix build --no-link -L path:.#ciJobs.aarch64-linux.<group>`.

### `x86_64-linux`

Inspect check capabilities and unsupported reasons, then build the hosted
non-runtime checks on a builder for this platform:

```sh
nix eval --json path:.#hostedCiPlan.x86_64-linux.inventory
nix build --no-link -L path:.#hostedCiJobs.x86_64-linux.checks
```

Buildable output groups: `checks`, `darwinConfigurations`, `devShells`, `formatters`, `homeConfigurations`, `nixosConfigurations`, `packages`.
Build one with `nix build --no-link -L path:.#ciJobs.x86_64-linux.<group>`.


`ciBundles.<system>` builds the full output projection, including checks
that hosted runners cannot execute. It is not the default local task.
Building a native application's package is not execution evidence, and
emulation is not native-platform evidence.

## Reproduce a runtime failure

For a registered NixOS runtime check, use the ordinary check build above.
If its source declares `__noChroot`, run the upstream `.driver` on an
appropriate disposable builder rather than weakening the Nix sandbox:

```sh
driver=$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths "path:.#checks.$system.$check.driver")
run_dir=$(mktemp -d /var/tmp/homelab-test.XXXXXX)
chmod 700 "$run_dir"
XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$run_dir" "$driver/bin/nixos-test-driver"
```

Drivers retain VM disks. Use disk-backed scratch, not `/run/user` tmpfs;
remove only your owned scratch after the driver and its VMs stop. Keep
sufficient disk and memory for the fixture's declared resources.

Native application commands below come from the same descriptors the
hosted executor uses. Run them only on their named native platform with
an exclusive disposable Docker daemon. Cleanup failure is a failure;
scoped, skipped or mutated runs are not full acceptance.



### `media-live-acceptance` on `x86_64-linux`

Executor requirements: `docker`.




```sh
nix run path:.#media-live-acceptance -- --docker-host unix:///var/run/docker.sock --platform linux/amd64
```

To use the hosted executor for a reviewed ref instead:

```sh
gh workflow run ci.yml --ref "$REF" -f system=x86_64-linux -f check=media-live-acceptance
```

### `household-sign-in-runtime` on `x86_64-linux`

Executor requirements: `docker`, `ownedStorage`, `root`.
The disposable executor must resolve `id.bzfx.net` to
`127.0.0.1`; the application does not edit host resolution.

Use an exclusive disposable runner with owned Docker and scratch storage,
never a shared daemon or a production host. Prefer the hosted executor,
which prepares this storage, over running the command on a workstation.



```sh
nix run path:.#household-sign-in-runtime --
```

To use the hosted executor for a reviewed ref instead:

```sh
gh workflow run ci.yml --ref "$REF" -f system=x86_64-linux -f check=household-sign-in-runtime
```

### `verify-kubernetes-api` on `x86_64-linux`

Executor requirements: `docker`.


Run in an owned evidence directory where `kubernetes-api-result.json` does
not already exist. Preserve the sanitized report, not fixture credentials
or raw logs.


```sh
nix run path:.#verify-kubernetes-api -- --docker-context default --report kubernetes-api-result.json
nix run path:.#verify-kubernetes-api -- --check-report kubernetes-api-result.json
```

To use the hosted executor for a reviewed ref instead:

```sh
gh workflow run ci.yml --ref "$REF" -f system=x86_64-linux -f check=verify-kubernetes-api
```


## Use hosted CI and inspect failures

Open a pull request for full verification. For a manual full run on a
reviewed ref, leave both selection inputs at their defaults:

```sh
gh workflow run ci.yml --ref "$REF"
```

Set `check` and `system` only to diagnose a selected registration. Manual
runs are diagnostic: they do not replace a PR's final required status or
publish helpers, even when every selected job passes.
In the Actions run, inspect the first failing job and its evidence
artifacts; a missing or skipped job is not passing evidence. Start with
collected sanitized reports. Remove credentials, kubeconfigs and workload
data before sharing additional diagnostics.

For Gateway prerequisite failures, inspect the sanitized
`gatewayPrerequisiteWitness` in the native report. Its categories are
hints, not a root-cause diagnosis; unavailable or unclassified results
remain unresolved. A witness does not replace the failed acceptance.

Keep output selection, capabilities and registration decisions in
[`modules/flake/ci.nix`](modules/flake/ci.nix), not check-name branches in
the workflow. [The workflow](.github/workflows/ci.yml) owns dispatch and
artifacts; [`required-ci.py`](.github/required-ci.py) owns their final
join. Maintainers must require the final `Required CI` status in branch
protection; repository source alone cannot configure that protection.

## Update workflow dependencies

After changing an action reference or adding a workflow, use GitHub's
[official locking tool](https://github.com/github/gh-actions-lock):

```sh
gh actions-lock --no-narrow --no-interactive
gh actions-lock --verify
```

Review the workflow and generated `.github/workflows/actions.lock`
together. Do not hand-edit the lockfile or accept a moved reference
merely to unblock CI. Locking covers action dependencies, including
nested actions; it does not pin container images, arbitrary downloads
or dependencies of external reusable workflows.

## Regenerate documentation

Edit the source, not its committed output. Documentation generators live
in [`modules/flake/docs/`](modules/flake/docs/); the household runbook is
generated by
[`operations.nix`](modules/den/aspects/kubernetes/operations.nix).
The [README overview](README.md) is handwritten.

From the intended checkout root:

```sh
nix run .#write-files
nix run .#diff-files
```

The writer updates generated files; the diff app reports drift without
writing. Both select the nearest Git checkout or JJ workspace, ignoring
inherited Git paths. They refuse to run outside a checkout.
Review every resulting change and track new generated files before
evaluating their checks.
Generated copies also have `checks.<system>."files/<path>"` freshness
checks. For example:

```sh
system=$(nix eval --impure --raw --expr builtins.currentSystem)
nix build --no-link -L "path:.#checks.$system.\"files/CI.md\""
```

## Deliver helper images

After an explicitly approved producer merge, wait for the ordinary main
push's required CI and helper candidate verification. PRs and selected
or manual runs do not publish candidates. Publication does not select
or deploy a new consumer image.

Follow [Deliver helper images](docs/operations/jellyfin.md#deliver-helper-images)
to review the verified artifact and open a separate consumer selection
PR. Keep immutable source/digest mappings and supported rollback images;
never replace a missing image with a mutable tag.

If a new package is private or lacks repository Actions access, obtain
separate owner authorization for its external package settings, then
rerun only the failed verification job, not a successful publisher.
Do not substitute a personal token or publish from an unreviewed branch.
Nix cache publication is separate and public: never include decrypted
secrets in any output.
